chat.text: How is this different from QUIC inside any tunnel protocol?  The entirety of of the QUIC headers would be hidden, no?

chat.text: This is not special.

chat.text: Of course, with QUIC on the tunnel itself, advice can be attached to the tunnel as a whole.

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: That signal is not something you want to rely on.

chat.text: scramble would be pretty tricky to get right with a long header packet

chat.text: Scone is an advisory signal special casing it in the rules for long header tunneling does not make sense to me.

chat.author: Ted Hardie
chat.text: The choice to use MASQUE is driven by the emitter, and over-riding it for network element convenience is inappropriate.

chat.author: Mike Bishop
chat.text: If a QAP wanted to, it could implement SCONE and mark the packets passing through the proxy.

chat.author: Ted Hardie
chat.text: Agreed, that works.

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: ...including SCONE stripping and re-adding on forwarded packets.

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: Though maybe that's not a great plan if you consider that the tunnel might carry multiple SCONE-using flows.  Because you'll add more SCONE overhead than you really need.

chat.author: Kazuho Oku
chat.text: for server -> client packets, the client needs to take min of the SCONE signals attached to the inner packet and the outer packet?

chat.author: Christian Huitema
chat.text: Decoalescing is already an issue during handshake, because packet length is important...

chat.author: Christian Huitema
chat.text: We should separate "basic" forwarding and "scone aware" tunneling.

chat.author: Christian Huitema
chat.text: Are you going to let Mirja speak?

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: Possible is a maybe, but your PMTUD will get whacky.

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: If your SCONE-marked packets are the same size as the forwarded packets, you might find that the SCONE ones don't fit the MTU.

chat.author: Christian Huitema
chat.text: Yes, the MTU is a real issue!

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: sconramble transform!

chat.author: Tommy Pauly

chat.text: The QUIC proxy is a server right?

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: for the tunnel, yes

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: You can't solve it by padding short header packets, unless you plan to add a long header packet to every short header packet...

chat.author: Martin Duke
chat.text: I don't think the default "breaks." The SH MTU is smaller than it needs to be

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: What if you probe up to the MTU on the short header packets?

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: The LH MTU is the small one.

chat.author: Tommy Pauly
chat.text: For the MTU, if the bottleneck is on the link with the proxy, and the LH packet actually wouldn't fit tunneled (which I think in practice might be rare), then there is always the option to put it over a non-datagram capsule.

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: I don't understand how that works, without the MTU thing Christian added.

chat.author: Tommy Pauly
chat.text: What's the issue with putting it over a capsule? (Note that PMTUD probes are short headers and thus are discovering the forwarded MTU)

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: Because you will discover PMTUD using short headers and that will be larger than the LH MTU, which will hit limits when you add a SCONE packet and encapsulation overhead.

chat.author: David Schinazi
chat.text: The scrambles would take non-trivial amounts of work to support long headers'

chat.author: Tommy Pauly
chat.text: Right, and if that happens and the LH doesn't fit in a QUIC datagram, you send it in a datagram capsule within the stream.

chat.author: Tommy Pauly
chat.text: (Agreed with David)

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: Oh, capsules have poor performance, but I guess they don't suffer from MTU caps.  Sorry, I was reading DATAGRAM frame.

chat.author: Tommy Pauly
chat.text: Yeah. You lose performance there if you go down that route, but I also think this would be quite quite rare in practice

chat.author: Tommy Pauly
chat.text: So we can call out that if it's not there already

chat.author: Christian Huitema
chat.text: Remember that SCone is supposed to be a few packets per 67seconds. Performance should not be all that critical.

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text:
Christian Huitema said:

Remember that SCone is supposed to be a few packets per 67seconds. Performance should not be all that critical.

Maybe not peformance for the SCONE signal, but presumably the packet it travels with has some latency sensitivity.

chat.author: David Schinazi
chat.text: If that's a concern it would be pretty easy to bundle SCONE with low-priority packets

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: Always?  Not all applications are aware of the existence of tunnels (which is the central issue).

chat.author: Martin Duke
chat.text: I guess there was an implicit assumption in QAP that there would be no long headers after a while, and now we've broken that

chat.author: Martin Thomson
chat.text: I'd prefer to have the MASQUE proxy provide a DOH resolver (or an ODOH relay and gateway and resolver...)

chat.text: What I was asking was not to change the protocol but maybe just add some discussion about the implications of having long headers in the middle of a quic flow. Yes it works but it could e.g. lead to re-ordering or delays especially if you use capsules over multiple packets.

chat.text: QAP makes bad assumptions about the things that will be tunneled.  Namely that they can be forwarded without any real downside.

chat.text: The problem is that the server won't not know that it is being tunneled, so it might send SCONE.  Because the client might not know that it is tunneled.

chat.text: The thing that puzzles me is that I thought the network segments close to a client are the places where I expected SCONE to help most and then is that part where MASQUE would hide the SCONE header?

chat.text: Yes but if the scone endpoint is also the masque endpoint that is fine. If that is not the case you might not be use scone. Your choice.

chat.text: When the Masque endpoint is the SCONE endpoint and the Masque endpoint does forwarding, where does it put its SCONE packets (it's not forwarding incoming SCONE packets, it's generating new ones).

chat.text: Going back to the discussion about QAP, does this need to more strongly enforce a single MTU regardless of compression savings?

chat.text: Yes, absolutely. Compression is a way to save bandwidth, but it should not introduce bugs.

chat.author: Martin Duke
chat.text: @marcus I think it has to move that packet into the tunnel. The datagram MTU has to be scaled so that the origin doesn't accidentally exceed it when prepending scone
